solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sit oddly posed, captured by rhythmically precise French painter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are held inside the phrase for rhythmically precise, as a captive is held

parts.note: keeping exact rhythm is being in time

indicators.note: posed in an odd way, so the three letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A model sits awkwardly for a French artist whose own work is metronomically exact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posed' looks like part of the modelling picture, but 'oddly posed' is the anagram signal giving IST; 'captured by' then holds IST inside the phrase IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimiste is one of a group of French painters, such as Vuillard and Bonnard, who painted quiet domestic interiors.

clue.text: Clip joint? Money raised before installing one

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word for money is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: the word for before takes the letter for one inside it, as a fitting is installed

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sleazy bar asks for cash up front before it lets a customer in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' (read upwards in a down clue) turns TIN into NIT; 'installing' puts I into ERE to make ERIE. A clip joint is a nightclub that overcharges, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A niterie is a nightclub, and a clip joint is a seedy nightclub that fleeces its patrons.

clue.text: Organ device tool adjusted, introducing rapid movement of a kind

indicators.note: the shuffled tool letters have the eye-movement letters brought into them
the letters of tool are adjusted, set into a different order

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, a kind of rapid movement in sleep

explanation.surface: An organ builder adjusts a part, making it vibrate quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' turns TOOL into TOLO; 'rapid movement of a kind' is the sleep kind, and 'introducing' sets it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is an organ stop or mechanism that makes the pitch waver.

clue.text: Lives for ever? That's surprising (4, two words)

parts.note: to live is to be, so lives gives is
ay (or aye) is an old and Scots word meaning always, for ever

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a person will never die and exclaims in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: AY meaning 'always' is the same word as the poetic 'for aye'.
explanation.definitionFit: I say is an exclamation of surprise, the same as saying that something is surprising.

clue.text: Small freshwater fish, otherwise found under the sea

indicators.note: in a down entry the alias letters sit below the sea letters

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean, the sea
aka, also known as, means otherwise called

explanation.surface: A little river fish is, oddly, discovered beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradicts itself, a freshwater fish under the sea; 'found under' just puts AKA below MED in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The medaka is a small Japanese killifish of rice paddies and streams, widely kept in aquariums.

clue.text: Female eagles heading south for Medway location

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
ernes are sea eagles

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here the first of south

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A group of female eagles is flying south towards a place in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' takes the first letter of south. Sheerness is a town in Kent on the Isle of Sheppey, where the River Medway meets the Thames estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The town stands at the mouth of the Medway, so it is a location on that river.

clue.text: Pigeon, disordered but not dead, on time

indicators.note: not dead means the letter for dead is dropped

parts.note: turbid can mean confused or disordered, as well as muddy

explanation.surface: A pigeon, flustered but alive, arrives punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disordered' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym, TURBID; 'not' drops its D for dead, leaving TURBI.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbit is a breed of domestic fancy pigeon with a short beak and a ruffled breast.

clue.text: Conifer coloured unfenced garden, variegated

indicators.note: variegated means mixed in pattern, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: C is a dictionary abbreviation for coloured

indicators.note: a word without its fence has lost its boundary letters, its first and last

parts.note: garden with its outer letters gone leaves its middle four

explanation.surface: A tree in an open, colourful garden of mixed planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfenced' strips GARDEN to ARDE; with C that gives CARDE, which 'variegated' mixes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is an evergreen cone-bearing tree, so it is a conifer.

clue.text: Tumour in part of anatomy (omasum)

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of anatomy into the start of omasum

explanation.surface: A growth is found in some region of the body, specifically a cow's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part of' signals a hidden word. The omasum is the third stomach of a ruminant.
explanation.definitionFit: A myoma is a benign growth made of muscle tissue, so a kind of tumour.

clue.text: Foster-mother abroad, mobile, given rations permit

parts.note: M is a dictionary abbreviation for mobile
an etape is a soldier's daily ration of food (and a stage of a march)
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A travelling carer overseas is issued with supplies and a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: ETAPE, from French, means both a day's march and the rations issued for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A metapelet is the Hebrew word for a woman who looks after children on a kibbutz, so a foster-mother in Israel.

clue.text: Ribes growing wild in part of Jock's stubble

indicators.note: growing wild, out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Currant bushes run riot in a Scottish stubble field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' signals the anagram; Ribes is the currant genus, which suits the plant picture, and 'Jock' signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Birse is Scots for a bristle, a single hair of the kind that makes up stubble.

clue.text: Sleep that's rapid coming upon the old

indicators.note: the rapid comes first and lands on the old article after it

parts.note: a shute (or chute) is a rapid, a fast-flowing stretch of river
ye is the old form of the

explanation.surface: A quick nap that overtakes an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rapid' reads as an adjective describing sleep but is the noun, a stretch of fast water; 'coming upon' puts it before YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is an informal word for sleep.

clue.text: Not quite sober? Help as before needed

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is left off

parts.note: steady can mean sober, not tipsy

explanation.surface: Someone a little tipsy needs the old kind of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts the last letter of STEADY; 'as before' marks an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead once meant help or assistance, a sense surviving in 'stand in good stead'.

clue.text: Jeweller's stone, unconcealed, I provide as inset

indicators.note: the pronoun and the verb are set in the middle of the word for unconcealed, as a gem is inset

parts.note: pert is an old word meaning open or evident, unconcealed
to do can mean to provide, as a cafe does lunches

explanation.surface: A jeweller openly offers to set a gem into a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconcealed' is the obsolete sense of pert, 'open, manifest', not 'cheeky'; 'as inset' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of olivine, used by jewellers.

clue.text: What'll attract attention and stifle news just breaking

parts.note: st is an interjection used to attract someone's attention
to oppress can mean to smother or stifle

explanation.surface: Something designed to grab notice and suppress stories as they emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests censorship; ST is a hiss like 'psst'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press is late news inserted into a newspaper after printing has begun.

clue.text: Body measurement

parts.note: read plainly: a measurement taken round part of the body; the setter's reading is the same: this is a bare definition with no wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: This is Azed's competition word: it is given only a plain definition, and readers send in their own cryptic clues for it, so there is no wordplay to find.
explanation.definitionFit: The waistline is the girth around the narrowest part of the trunk, measured for clothing.

clue.text: Intrinsic part of erotica, mainly?

indicators.note: an intrinsic part lies within, so the answer is inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of erotica and the start of mainly

explanation.surface: Asks what lies at the heart of most erotic writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intrinsic part of' signals a hidden word; read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cama, a variant of kama, is earthly desire or love, the very stuff of erotic writing.

clue.text: Skill backing with bloke on board horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: the bloke climbs on board, inside the reversed word
backing means going backwards, so the letters for skill are reversed

parts.note: art is skill
an oik is a loutish bloke

explanation.surface: A lout clambers backwards onto a carriage pulled by horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ART into TRA, and 'on board' seats the bloke inside it; oik is British slang for an uncouth person.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Wretched nag having to carry away old foundation material

parts.note: a rip is a worthless horse
rap is an obsolete verb meaning to carry away or transport, the root of rapt

explanation.surface: A poor old horse made to haul away ancient building stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are Chambers senses; 'old' marks RAP as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Riprap is loose broken stone used as a foundation or to protect embankments.

clue.text: A pointilliste may spatter tile with these

definitions.text: A pointilliste may spatter tile with these

indicators.note: spattering throws the letters about, so they come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A dot painter could flick colours onto a tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may spatter' works on A POINTILLISTE, whose letters are those of TILE plus the answer; take TILE out and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointillist painter applies dots of pigment, typically oil-based colours, so these are the medium.

clue.text: Nutritional component in wine cheers artery

indicators.note: the thanks and the road go in the French word for wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine
ta, like cheers, is British informal thanks
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, an arterial road; MI reads as M1

explanation.surface: A health ingredient found in wine, toasting the circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, and an artery is a major road, so a numeral reads as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in small amounts in the diet.

clue.text: Partner, single, in Italian ball game

parts.note: a pal is a friend or partner
lone means single, solitary

explanation.surface: A mate, unattached, takes part in a sport in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallone is an old Italian game in which a large ball is struck with a wooden armguard.

clue.text: Sob freely, fit when interring one — in such …

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters move about
interring means burying, so the letter for one is buried inside the word for fit

parts.note: equal means fit, as in equal to the task
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mourner weeps openly at a burial.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the next clue: 'in such … funeral rites'. 'freely' turns SOB into OBS, and 'when interring' buries I in EQUAL to give EQUIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequial means relating to obsequies, the rites of a funeral.

clue.text: Sharp turn fastening cable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: acrid or harsh in taste
second meaning: a turn of a ship's cable round the bitts, the posts on deck

explanation.walkthrough: The nautical sense comes from the bitts, the pair of posts on which a cable is made fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means harsh-tasting, and on a ship it names a round of rope taken round mooring posts.

clue.text: The old move to crouch low removing cap before church

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: to squat is to crouch low

explanation.surface: An old person shifts to squat down, doffing a hat before entering church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing cap' takes the S off SQUAT, leaving QUAT. QUATCH is Shakespearean, hence 'The old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quatch is an obsolete verb meaning to stir or budge.

clue.text: … Funeral rites, led by priest? Statistician's unit

indicators.note: the rites come after the priest, who leads

parts.note: obit is an old word for funeral rites or a memorial service

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: last rites headed by a cleric, then the twist to statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by' puts PR in front. 'Funeral rites' does double duty, finishing the definition of the previous clue as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A probit is a unit of probability used in statistics, based on deviation from the mean of a normal distribution.

clue.text: What stationer stocks: rubber for use in centre of carrel

indicators.note: the rubber is put for use inside the middle letters
the centre of a six-letter word is its two middle letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of carrel
ule is a Central American rubber tree, or its rubber

explanation.surface: A stationery shop stocks erasers for library study booths.
explanation.walkthrough: A carrel is a study cubicle in a library, whose 'centre of' gives RR; 'rubber' looks like an eraser but names a rubber tree, which 'for use in' sets inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler for measuring and drawing lines is standard stationery stock.

clue.text: Brave, perhaps, ignoring first bit of medicine?

indicators.note: the first bit is the first letter, which is left out

parts.note: a dosage is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is courageous to skip their medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring first bit' drops the D. 'Brave' is a noun here, a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people; a brave is one of their warriors.

clue.text: Sell stores to soldiers, crafty as of old

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to act as a sutler, a camp follower selling provisions
second meaning: an old spelling of subtle, cunning

explanation.walkthrough: The verb is a back-formation from sutler.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sutler's trading and an archaic spelling of an adjective meaning cunning.

clue.text: Druggie's back to front dodge

indicators.note: the back letter of the word moves to its front

parts.note: a user is a drug taker; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: An addict's trick of switching things round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the last letter only, not a full reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem, a dodge.

clue.text: Ballet character, cunning, escaping home of fabled monster

indicators.note: the monster's home escapes, leaving the word

parts.note: wiliness is cunning
Loch Ness is home of the legendary monster

explanation.surface: A wily dancer flees the Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' removes NESS: Loch Ness in Scotland is the supposed home of the Loch Ness monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The wilis are the ghostly maidens of Giselle, so a Wili is a character in that ballet.

clue.text: Protein in e.g. tendons entails flexing

indicators.note: flexing bends the word, so its letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Stretching your tendons involves a particular protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is the elastic protein in connective tissue such as tendons and arteries.

clue.text: Misanthrope making money in a jiffy? The opposite

indicators.note: the in of money in a jiffy places one word inside the other
the opposite way round, so the jiffy goes inside the money

parts.note: tin is slang for money
a mo is a moment, a jiffy

explanation.surface: A hater of humanity who gets rich in no time, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'in' puts money inside a jiffy; 'The opposite' swaps the roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, in Shakespeare's play, is the classic hater of mankind.

clue.text: Divide up FBI agents in group

indicators.note: the agents are placed in the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men are government agents of the FBI

explanation.surface: The Bureau splits its agents into teams.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment is to split into parts, the same as to divide up.

clue.text: Nick, college joiner

parts.note: a link joins two things

explanation.surface: A student called Nick joins a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Clink is slang for prison, as is nick, so both mean jail.

clue.text: Brain surgeon, maybe, reverse of brisk in cutting into this lady

indicators.note: the word for brisk is turned the other way

parts.note: pert can mean brisk or lively

indicators.note: the little word cuts into the pronoun, sitting inside it

parts.note: her refers to this lady

explanation.surface: A surgeon briskly operates on a woman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns brisk's synonym into TREP. The clue's 'in' is a letter piece, not a link: 'cutting into' places it inside 'this lady' to make HINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trephiner bores holes in the skull with a trephine, as a brain surgeon may.
